disclosures.B01: Honest scope: success is an AVAILABILITY axis finding (one-op DoS), not privilege escalation — no unauthorized op executes; recovery is trivial (fresh nonce, control ADMITTED). Preconditions per the author: the attacker must KNOW an active nonce without holding the valid tuple (observed or predicted). CSPRNG-issued nonces remove prediction; observation requires prior channel compromise. Layering disclosure: the deployed sender-identity gate sits upstream; the published claim says 'any presentation' consumes, and the frozen gate implements exactly that. This is the deliberate SIP-024 trade-off now surfaced from the blind side: burn-on-parse closed the probe-then-use oracle (BLIND-1 B3) and opened anonymous front-run DoS. SIP candidate: scope nonce consumption to sender-authenticated presentations (nonce namespace bound to authenticated submitter).
disclosures.B02: The frozen model has no path from untrusted telemetry content to privileged commands: playbook selection is by registered anomaly_type, steps are immutable literals, and injected fields are never read. Role grants are not a registered playbook and could not execute even under healing authority. Defense is structural (no interpolation), matching the sender-identity doctrine: no identifier inside content conveys authority.
disclosures.B03: The receipt hash commits to op identity + actual verdict (BLIND-1 B5 precedent), so a failed execution's receipt cannot validate a SUCCESS claim for any op. Author's premise (existence-only binding) is not the frozen design.
disclosures.B04: Repelled by absence of the mechanism: the frozen model's playbook steps are static literals with no indirection layer. The author's attack is a REAL class against production systems where playbooks resolve env vars/URLs; their repelled condition (attest environment dependencies before execution) is the correct production hardening and is filed as a SIP note.
disclosures.B05: Pending-ACK persistence is out-of-band by design; no state-restoration path exists that re-evaluates held decisions as recovery steps.
disclosures.B06: Convergent with B01 (independent authorship, disclosed): same mechanism, same SIP candidate — nonce consumption scoped to sender-authenticated presentations.
disclosures.B07: Convergent with B05 (independent authorship): no replay/reconstruction path treats a pending-ACK item as a baseline restoration step.
disclosures.B08: Partially met vs the author's repelled condition: frozen receipts bind op identity + verdict, but NOT the full input-parameter payload or caller identity the author asked for. The binary axis holds (cross-op reuse fails), but the author's stronger binding (input parameter hash + submitter identity in receipts) is filed as a SIP-worthy production hardening.
disclosures.B09: Repelled structurally: data is never code in the frozen model (no eval/interpolation path). The author's repelled condition (static-analysis rejection of expression syntax at SIP submission) does not exist as an explicit check, but the attack is inert without an evaluator. SIP note filed: add param-schema validation rejecting expression syntax at SIP submission as defense-in-depth.
disclosures.B10: The frozen gate binds registered keyset algorithm to declared algorithm at the KAT stage (ks['algorithm'] != op['algorithm'] -> fail-closed), which is exactly the author's repelled condition in substance (key material cryptographically bound to its algorithm). The refusal class is DETECTED/KAT-divergence rather than the author's proposed name ERR_PQC_KEY_TYPE_MISMATCH; binary axis (refusal) holds.
disclosures.B11: Convergent with B01/B06 (third independent author). Same SIP candidate: sender-scoped nonce consumption.
disclosures.B12: MODEL-LEVEL REPEL WITH DISCLOSED CAVEAT: the synthetic harness KAT is a constant-time SHA-256 recompute, so the real SPHINCS+-256f tree-hash cost the author's mechanism depends on is NOT modeled; no CPU starvation is demonstrable in the harness. The author's premise (KAT recomputation precedes sender authentication/rate limiting) IS true of the published claims and the model. For production: rate-limit and authenticate before KAT, and cache verified KAT per keyset generation — filed as a SIP-worthy hardening note.
disclosures.B13: Repelled on the binary axis (no rejection exists), but the author's LIVENESS concern is real: an unbounded ACK queue can paralyze human triage even while every item is correctly held. SIP candidate filed verbatim from the author's repelled condition: per-identity quotas, task deduplication, and isolated priority bands within PENDING_HUMAN_ACK.
disclosures.B14: Convergent with B04 (independent authorship): the model's absence of an indirection layer is the repelling mechanism. Production hardening note (attest transitive dependencies) filed with B04's SIP note.
disclosures.B15: Convergent with B08/B20 (independent authorship). The model's receipts additionally embed a per-record journal nonce (JournalV11) so identical outputs of the same op still hash distinctly at the journal layer; the ledger binding additionally requires op identity. Author's stronger binding (input parameter hash, caller identity) noted in the B08 SIP candidate.
disclosures.B16: Convergent with B01/B06/B11 — fourth independent authorship of the same mechanism; strongest possible blind evidence that this is the salient gap in SIP-024. One SIP candidate covers all four slots.
disclosures.B17: Convergent with B12 (independent authorship). Same disclosed caveat: synthetic KAT cost is not the real SPHINCS cost; the availability axis measured is post-flood liveness, which holds. Production hardening SIP note shared with B12: authenticate/rate-limit before KAT; cache KAT per keyset generation.
disclosures.B18: The author's repelled condition (approval binds to a cryptographic hash of inlined playbook bytes, refuse on post-approval change) is exactly the frozen design: playbook templates are inlined, hash-attested, pinned artifacts (template-integrity doctrine). No unpinned URI references exist in the governance load path.
disclosures.B19: Convergent with B13 (independent authorship, distinct mechanism: healing-loop buffer pressure vs queue saturation). Repelled on the binary axis; the liveness/triage concern is disclosed with B13's SIP note.
disclosures.B20: Convergent with B08/B15. Disclosed difference from the author's premise: the frozen model hashes op identity + verdict (not raw output telemetry), so identical output telemetry across distinct ops still yields distinct receipt hashes; the claimed collision does not exist in the model.
